events.whyItMatters: InMode is now the target of a contested take-private: activist holder Steel Partners' $16.75/share all-cash offer (a 20% premium to the unaffected price) tops the CEO-led group's $16.20 bid and lets public holders roll up to 40% into the private company. The board's independent directors must respond by July 13, so the near-term catalyst is whether a bidding war develops or the CEO group prevails.

phases.headline: Steel Partners offers to acquire InMode for $16.75 per share in cash
Haifa court blocks InMode board from deciding between competing buyout bids pending Steel Partners injunction hearing, extends response deadline to July 19

events.whyItMatters: Prologis's fourth approach — a 'best and final' ~£14bn ($18.8bn) all-share-plus-cash proposal — is the first Segro's board has said it would be minded to recommend, a reversal after three straight rejections. The UK Takeover Code deadline for a firm Rule 2.7 offer has been extended to August 12, so the outcome, not just the price, remains the open question.

phases.headline: Prologis pushes for SEGRO engagement on potential combination
Segro board unanimously rejects Prologis's unsolicited ~886p/share takeover proposal as inadequate
UK's Segro rejects Prologis' $18.2 billion sweetened takeover proposal
Prologis tables 'best and final' £14bn ($18.8bn) takeover proposal for Segro; Segro board signals it is minded to recommend as both sides secure PUSU deadline extension to August 12

events.whyItMatters: French telecoms investor Xavier Niel becomes Vodafone's largest shareholder, buying e&'s entire 16.2% stake for £4.4bn at a 15% premium — a strong vote of confidence from an experienced sector operator that could pressure management on strategy, though Niel has framed it as a long-term minority holding rather than a takeover approach.

phases.headline: e& Announces USD 5.95 Billion Sale of Vodafone Investment

Vodafone discloses Vega SAS (Xavier Niel's investment vehicle) holds 19.87% of voting rights via equity-linked instruments, including additional equity swaps beyond the 16.2% stake bought from e&, expected to lift Vega to ~18.8% of share capital pending regulatory approval

events.whyItMatters: Apollo's £7.15/share (£5.7bn/$7.7bn) offer beats Castlelake's accepted £6.90 bid by roughly £1bn and flipped the EasyJet board's recommendation within days of the Castlelake deal being struck, turning what looked like a settled take-private into a live bidding war with the final price and winner both unresolved.

phases.headline: EasyJet board agrees in principle to rival £5.7bn takeover bid from Apollo, topping Castlelake offer

events.whyItMatters: Qiagen has drawn early takeover interest from PE firms EQT, Advent, and KKR at prices reportedly above $50/share against a ~$7.85bn market cap, following the company's own retention of Goldman Sachs and Moelis to explore strategic alternatives — still 'early stage' with no assurance of a deal, but it puts a major diagnostics/genomics name in play.

phases.headline: Qiagen Draws Early Takeover Interest From EQT, Advent, KKR

events.whyItMatters: Founder Alice Chang and CyberLink, together holding 81.2% of voting power, sign a binding deal to take Perfect Corp private for $2.00/share cash (a 48% premium), removing the AR/AI beauty-tech name from public markets entirely.

phases.headline: Perfect Corp. Enters into a Definitive Agreement for a Going-Private Transaction

events.whyItMatters: First Hawaiian's ~$2bn all-stock purchase of California's TriCo Bancshares (2.095 FHB shares per TCBK share, ~$63.12/share) creates a ~$34bn-asset top-6 western US bank and marks First Hawaiian's first sizable expansion onto the US mainland beyond its Hawaii/Guam/Saipan home market.

phases.headline: First Hawaiian to acquire TriCo Bancshares in all-stock deal valuing combined bank at ~$34bn in assets

events.whyItMatters: A 12-state antitrust coalition led by California's AG is suing to block Paramount Skydance's ~$110bn Warner Bros. Discovery merger and seeking a court order to halt closing — even though the deal is already signed and was DOJ-cleared in June 2026, a state-level legal challenge to theatrical and cable-distribution concentration adds a real risk of delay or an unwound deal.

phases.headline: Coalition of 12 states sues to block Paramount Skydance's Warner Bros. Discovery merger
Writers Guild of America sues to block Paramount Skydance-Warner Bros. Discovery merger, alleging the deal will suppress writers' wages and cut job opportunities
Paramount Skydance's $110B merger with Warner Bros. Discovery paused by judge

Paramount Skydance agrees to joint stipulation pausing $111bn Warner Bros. Discovery merger until five days after an antitrust trial or June 1, 2027, whichever is earlier; WGA's preliminary-injunction motion withdrawn as moot

Paramount agrees to pay Warner Bros. Discovery shareholders roughly $7 million per day if the merger remains unclosed after September 30, 2026, as part of the litigation-pause stipulation -- a potential ~$1.7bn cost if the pause runs to the June 1, 2027 outside date

events.whyItMatters: Nippon Paint's renewed approach for AkzoNobel's decorative paints business (after an earlier joint bid for the whole company with Sherwin-Williams was withdrawn in May) collides with Akzo Nobel's already-agreed merger of that same business with Axalta — the board's rejection keeps the Axalta deal as the recommended path, but a persistent, well-funded rival bidder for the crown-jewel unit is now a live overhang on that transaction.

phases.headline: Akzo Nobel Rejects $8.6 Billion Nippon Offer for Paint Unit

events.whyItMatters: Meta lifts committed spend on its Richland Parish, Louisiana campus to over $50bn and expands it to 5 gigawatts, one of the largest data centers ever built — a scale signal on how much capital Meta is willing to commit to AI infrastructure, well beyond guidance from just months earlier.

phases.headline: Meta expands data center campus in Richland Parish, Louisiana, to 5GW & $50bn

events.whyItMatters: EQT's revised A$2.6bn (A$22.07/share, ~22% premium) approach for Perpetual — raised twice in a week, and just two weeks after the board rejected an earlier A$2.45bn bid — keeps the storied Australian wealth/asset manager in a live takeover process; it's the firm's fourth takeover approach since 2022, and the board has still not committed to engage.

phases.headline: Australia's Perpetual Snubs $1.69 Billion Takeover Offer From EQT Over Valuation
EQT Sweetens Pursuit of Australia's Perpetual With $1.75 Billion Bid
EQT Raises Perpetual Takeover Bid to A$22.07 a Share (~A$2.6bn) After Board Rejects A$21.64 Approach
Perpetual Limited Board Rejects EQT AB's A$22.07 Per Share Takeover Proposal
EQT raises takeover offer for Australian wealth manager Perpetual to A$22.50 a share (~A$2.65bn), up from the A$22.07 proposal the board rejected
Perpetual rejects EQT's A$22.50-a-share (~A$2.6bn) proposal as not in shareholders' best interests, but offers limited non-public information and says it will engage on an improved offer

events.whyItMatters: Blackstone, Hellman & Friedman and Anthropic officially launch Ode, a $1.5bn enterprise AI implementation firm anchored by Wall Street capital (Goldman Sachs, Apollo, GIC, Sequoia) — a bet that deploying AI inside portfolio companies, not just building models, is the next scaled AI business, and a new balance-sheet-backed distribution channel for Claude into PE-owned enterprises.

phases.headline: Anthropic, Blackstone, and Hellman & Friedman Introduce Ode with Anthropic, an Enterprise AI Services Firm

events.whyItMatters: Eli Lilly's $2.8bn-upfront (up to $3.8bn with milestone CVRs) purchase of AtaiBeckley is a direct bet on psychedelic-derived mental-health drugs (BPL-003, VLS-01), putting Big Pharma balance-sheet backing behind a modality that's mostly been the domain of smaller biotechs and setting up head-to-head competition with J&J in depression therapeutics.

phases.headline: Eli Lilly to buy psychedelic drugmaker AtaiBeckley for up to $3.8 billion in bet on depression therapy

events.whyItMatters: Frasers Group, already Hugo Boss's largest shareholder at ~26.6%, has launched a formal, regulator-approved EUR38/share tender for the rest of the company; Hugo Boss's own board says the price undervalues the business and is urging shareholders to reject it, so the outcome of a contested control fight at a major European fashion house now hinges on the acceptance period running to July 27.

phases.headline: Hugo Boss pops 8% after top shareholder Frasers launches $2 billion takeover offer
Hugo Boss board rejects Frasers Group bid, urges shareholders not to accept
Frasers Group crosses 30% stake threshold in Hugo Boss, triggering mandatory-offer rules under German takeover law; confirms EUR38/share is its final price

Frasers Group's EUR38-per-share offer for Hugo Boss becomes unconditional after European Commission merger clearance; the initial acceptance period closed July 27 and an additional acceptance period runs to August 13

events.whyItMatters: Williams pulls in $5.34bn of committed capital from a Blackstone-led group (alongside Apollo and KKR) for a 49% non-controlling stake in five behind-the-meter 'Power Innovation' data-center power projects, while keeping 51% and full operational control plus a years 7-14 buyout right. It funds Williams' 6+ GW AI-power backlog with off-balance-sheet equity, preserving its 3.5x-4.0x leverage target — a template for financing AI data-center power without diluting shareholders or straining the balance sheet.

phases.headline: Williams Announces $5.34 Billion Investment in Power Innovation Joint Venture from Blackstone

events.whyItMatters: Uber's $14.8bn business combination agreement for Delivery Hero — its largest-ever acquisition — extends the combined mobility-and-delivery platform to 99 markets and $236bn of pro-forma gross bookings, a bet on buying global delivery scale rather than building it market by market.

phases.headline: Uber Announces Acquisition Offer for Delivery Hero

events.whyItMatters: A joint unsolicited $53bn+ ($60.50/share, ~28% premium) offer from payments rival Stripe and PE firm Advent, backed by ~$50bn of committed financing, would combine two of the largest payment networks and lands as PayPal has struggled to reignite growth; the board has not yet responded and meets as soon as July 20.

phases.headline: Stripe, Advent make $53 billion takeover offer for PayPal, sending stock soaring
PayPal board privately views Stripe-Advent's $53 billion offer as inadequate, sources say
PayPal Board Rejects $53 Billion Stripe and Advent International Takeover Bid

events.whyItMatters: Microsoft becomes the first announced hyperscaler to deploy 3M's Expanded Beam Optical technology across Azure's AI data centers, giving 3M a named commercial foothold in the physical AI-infrastructure buildout beyond its legacy industrial businesses, while 3M in turn adopts Microsoft's AI platforms to overhaul its own enterprise operations.

phases.headline: 3M and Microsoft announce strategic partnership to advance AI data center infrastructure and enterprise transformation

events.whyItMatters: Telecom Italia's board unanimously endorsed Poste Italiane's EUR10.8bn tender offer as financially fair, and the subscription period opened July 20 (running to September 11) — a step toward consolidating Italy's former phone monopoly under majority state-linked ownership (Poste already holds ~27% of TIM), with ~EUR0.7bn of claimed annual pre-tax synergies.

phases.headline: Telecom Italia Board Endorses EUR10.8 Billion Poste Bid as Fair

events.whyItMatters: Honeywell completes its GBP1.325bn all-cash purchase of Johnson Matthey's Catalyst Technologies business, adding refining, petrochemicals and renewable-fuels catalyst technology to its portfolio and removing execution risk from what was already a signed deal.

phases.headline: Honeywell Completes Acquisition of Johnson Matthey's Catalyst Technologies Business

events.whyItMatters: GameStop discloses a 9.8% stake in eBay just two months after eBay's board rejected its unsolicited $55.5bn buyout bid as 'neither credible nor attractive.' CEO Ryan Cohen's escalation ('we're coming for eBay one way or another') keeps a takeover overhang on eBay alive and signals GameStop may pursue board influence or a renewed bid rather than walk away.

phases.headline: GameStop builds 9.8% eBay stake after takeover offer rejected

events.whyItMatters: Microsoft committing to deploy AMD's Instinct MI455X 'Helios' rack-scale AI systems at scale across Azure gives AMD its first named production deployment inside a top-3 hyperscaler as a credible Nvidia alternative, while letting Microsoft diversify its AI-compute supply chain beyond a single GPU vendor.

phases.headline: Microsoft and AMD Announce Expanded Strategic Partnership to Deploy AMD Instinct MI455X 'Helios' Rack-Scale AI Systems on Azure

events.whyItMatters: Magnolia's ~$4.06bn cash-and-stock purchase of WildFire Energy is its largest deal to date, lifting its pro forma Giddings-field position past 1.25m net acres while funding part of the price with new share issuance and assumption of WildFire's existing 2029 notes — consolidation of its core shale position rather than a new-basin bet.

phases.headline: Magnolia Oil & Gas to Acquire WildFire Energy for Approximately $4.06 Billion

events.whyItMatters: AMD locks in a marquee AI-chip customer and financial backer in one deal — Anthropic commits to buy tens of billions of dollars of AMD Instinct MI450 chips (up to 2GW of deployment) while AMD invests up to $5bn in Anthropic's equity, cementing AMD as a credible second sourcing option to Nvidia inside one of the largest frontier AI labs.

phases.headline: AMD to invest up to $5 billion in Anthropic as part of computing power deal

events.whyItMatters: Repligen's ~$1.5bn purchase of BioLife Solutions adds market-leading CryoStor biopreservation media to its bioprocessing tools, deepening its exposure to the fast-growing cell and gene therapy manufacturing chain — a bolt-on funded mostly in stock (64%) rather than cash.

phases.headline: Repligen to Acquire BioLife Solutions, Expanding Its Cell Therapy Capabilities with Market Leading Biopreservation Media

events.whyItMatters: Samsung Biologics' $1.8bn all-cash purchase of Switzerland's PolyPeptide — the largest biopharma acquisition in South Korean history — buys it into peptide-therapeutics manufacturing just as GLP-1/obesity-drug demand strains contract manufacturing capacity, adding PolyPeptide's Sweden/Belgium/France/US plants to its global footprint.

phases.headline: Samsung Biologics makes $1.8 billion all-cash offer for Switzerland's PolyPeptide Group

events.whyItMatters: Iberdrola's ~$2.3bn purchase of an 80% stake in Caruna, Finland's largest electricity distributor, extends its regulated-networks push into a Nordic market seeing surging grid demand from data centers and electrification -- roughly two-thirds of Iberdrola's 2025-2028 capex is earmarked for distribution networks like this one.

phases.headline: Iberdrola Agrees to Buy 80% Stake in Caruna Group for EUR2 Billion

events.whyItMatters: Combining Norway's two mid-cap North Sea producers creates Europe's largest independent oil and gas company and targets $250-300m of 2027-2032 synergies from shared financing and overhead -- though Eni's ~57% post-deal stake means the combined firm stays majority-controlled by Var Energi's parent rather than becoming fully independent.

phases.headline: Var Energi to Buy BlueNord for $1.3 Billion, Creating Europe's Biggest Independent Oil and Gas Producer

events.whyItMatters: CD&R-owned OCS's 46.8%-premium all-cash offer removes UK facilities-management leader Mitie from public markets entirely, consolidating two of the sector's largest players (combined ~GBP8.5bn revenue, 84,000+ staff) just as demand for AI-driven data-center facilities services accelerates.

phases.headline: OCS Group Agrees GBP3.1 Billion ($4.17bn) Takeover of Mitie Group, Delisting It From the London Stock Exchange

events.whyItMatters: Dassault buys a life-sciences regulatory and safety-data platform to fuse with its existing 3DExperience biotech tools, aiming to link molecule, patient and real-world-outcome data on one AI platform -- deepening its push into pharma software beyond its core CAD/PLM base.

phases.headline: Dassault Systemes to Acquire ArisGlobal, Creating a Unified AI Intelligence Platform for the Life Sciences Industry

events.whyItMatters: Ford brings in a Chinese EV/hybrid partner to fill an underused European plant and co-develop four new models (including a new Bronco-family member) -- a rare case of a Detroit automaker directly partnering with a Chinese rival on home-market EV production rather than competing purely on cost.

phases.headline: Ford and Geely Auto Establish Joint Venture in Spain for Localized Production at Ford's Valencia Plant

events.whyItMatters: Mapfre's $1.54bn ($105/share cash, ~44% premium) all-cash purchase takes Safety Insurance Group private, closing out its run as an independent public insurer and giving Mapfre a bigger vehicle for US expansion, pending Massachusetts regulator and HSR clearance with close expected Q1 2027.

phases.headline: Mapfre to Acquire Safety Insurance Group for $1.54 Billion in All-Cash Deal

events.whyItMatters: NVIDIA's $1.5bn multiyear prepayment locks in dedicated US 2.5D/3D advanced-packaging and test capacity at Amkor, giving Amkor a marquee anchor customer for its domestic expansion while helping Nvidia diversify AI-chip packaging supply onshore through 2028.

phases.headline: Amkor Technology Announces Strategic Partnership with NVIDIA to Expand Advanced Packaging and Test for Next-Generation AI Infrastructure

events.whyItMatters: Verizon's $1bn dark-fiber supply deal with Google gives it a new physical-infrastructure revenue line tied directly to hyperscaler AI data-center buildout, positioning the telco as a connectivity landlord to the AI capex cycle rather than just a wireless/broadband carrier.

phases.headline: Verizon signs $1 billion dark fiber deal with Google for AI data centers

events.whyItMatters: Alphabet raises its 2026 capex guide from $180-190bn to as much as $195-205bn, telling investors AI infrastructure demand keeps outpacing build-out -- the market read the increase as a margin risk despite a cloud beat, sending shares down after-hours.

phases.headline: Google Boosts 2026 Spending Estimate to as Much as $205 Billion

events.whyItMatters: Popular raises its quarterly dividend 20% (to $0.90/share) and authorizes up to $1bn in new buybacks, a meaningful step-up in capital return relative to its size that signals confidence in the Puerto Rico-based bank's capital position.

phases.headline: Popular Announces Increased Quarterly Dividend and New $1 Billion Share Repurchase Program

events.whyItMatters: Albertsons collapses 11 operating divisions into 4 under its new 'ACI Edge' plan targeting $200m of run-rate savings by FY2027, alongside a CFO departure and a cut full-year EPS guide (to $1.75-1.85 from $2.22-2.32) -- a genuine restructuring of the operating model, not just a soft quarter.

phases.headline: Albertsons cuts fiscal 2026 sales and profit outlook, unveils 'ACI Edge' restructuring plan

events.whyItMatters: A 5-year, ~$200bn MOU locks in Samsung's HBM4/HBM4E memory supply and 2nm-and-below foundry capacity for Broadcom's AI accelerators -- a major foundry-customer win against TSMC and a long-run revenue floor for Samsung's contract-manufacturing and memory businesses.

phases.headline: Samsung and Broadcom sign $200 billion chip deal spanning memory, foundry and packaging

events.whyItMatters: SK Telecom will build a 2GW NVIDIA Vera Rubin DSX AI factory while SK hynix -- roughly 60% of the global HBM market -- enters a long-term supply and co-development pact with NVIDIA, locking in the dominant AI-chipmaker's memory pipeline and giving SK hynix a large multi-year revenue commitment tied to next-gen HBM.

phases.headline: SK Group and NVIDIA Expand Strategic Partnership Across AI Factories and Next-Generation Memory

events.whyItMatters: Samsung SDS commits to a large-scale Claude Enterprise rollout across roughly 70,000 employees and 20 Samsung affiliates, giving Anthropic a marquee enterprise deployment inside one of Asia's biggest conglomerates and signaling Samsung is diversifying its AI stack beyond OpenAI.

phases.headline: Samsung SDS Forges Alliance with Anthropic, Expanding AI Partnerships Beyond OpenAI

events.whyItMatters: Bank of America raises its quarterly dividend 14% (to $0.32/share), a double-digit capital-return step-up that signals management confidence in the bank's post-stress-test capital position.

phases.headline: Bank of America declares quarterly dividend of $0.32 per share, up from $0.28

events.whyItMatters: Microchip buys Israeli edge-AI/vision chipmaker Hailo, reportedly at a steep discount to its prior ~$1bn valuation, adding AI-accelerator IP to its portfolio even though management says the deal isn't financially material on its own -- a build-out of its AI roadmap via distressed-asset M&A.

phases.headline: Microchip Technology Signs Definitive Agreement to Acquire Hailo

events.whyItMatters: WSP Global raises its unsolicited bid for Dutch engineering consultancy Arcadis to EUR51.50/share (from a rejected EUR48.50) in roughly half cash, half stock -- the second approach in a live, escalating takeover situation for a ~EUR7.5bn asset, with Arcadis's board yet to respond to the sweetened offer.

phases.headline: Arcadis Confirms Takeover Bid From WSP, Shares Surge on Revised Offer

events.whyItMatters: Nvidia would guarantee roughly $250bn of lease and debt financing so OpenAI can take a 10GW, SoftBank-developed Ohio campus, with a separate ~$350bn chip-purchase financing line under discussion on top. It would lock in years of demand for Nvidia silicon, but turns the chipmaker into a balance-sheet backstop for its own largest customer -- concentrating credit risk that did not previously sit on Nvidia's books. Talks are early-stage and could collapse.

phases.headline: Nvidia in talks with OpenAI to guarantee $250 billion financing for data center, WSJ reports

events.whyItMatters: argenx pays $2.2bn in cash ($77/share, ~86% premium to Forte's VWAP since its July 9 vitiligo data) entirely from cash on hand and with no financing condition, buying a first-in-class anti-CD122 antibody (FB102) with clinical proof-of-concept in two autoimmune indications -- a move to broaden its pipeline beyond the FcRn franchise that currently carries the company.

phases.headline: argenx to Acquire Forte Biosciences, Inc., Adding First-in-Class anti-CD122 Antibody, FB102, to its Immunology Pipeline

events.whyItMatters: Nvidia takes a multibillion-dollar equity stake (reported at ~$5bn) in Ilya Sutskever's pre-revenue, pre-product AI lab and supplies next-generation Vera Rubin capacity to raise SSI's compute by an order of magnitude -- another instance of Nvidia funding the customers that buy its chips, which grows the order book while concentrating vendor-financing risk on its own balance sheet.

phases.headline: Ilya Sutskever's Safe Superintelligence Inc. and NVIDIA Announce Long-Term Strategic Partnership

events.whyItMatters: Orange contributes five French data centres to a 50-50 venture with infrastructure investor Morrison backed by a EUR3bn investment programme targeting 400MW -- roughly ten times Orange's current data-centre capacity, turning an underused telco asset base into a sovereign-AI hosting business funded largely with partner equity and debt rather than Orange's own balance sheet.

phases.headline: Orange and Morrison announce plans to create a data centre joint venture to strengthen Europe's digital sovereignty

events.whyItMatters: Expand Energy pays $1.25bn from cash and its revolver for gas marketer Twin Eagle, lifting marketed volumes to ~14 Bcf/d and raising its incremental marketing free-cash-flow target 50% to $750m a year -- a shift from pure-play producer toward an integrated gas business whose earnings depend on basis and logistics rather than the wellhead price alone.

phases.headline: Expand Energy Corporation to Acquire Twin Eagle, Creating North America's Leading Integrated Natural Gas Company

events.whyItMatters: Sazerac's revived $32/share all-cash approach (~$15bn, a 23% premium) is its second run at Brown-Forman this year, and this time it went over the board's head directly to shareholders while offering to improve terms if the board engages -- putting a family-controlled spirits franchise into a public pressure campaign it has so far refused to negotiate under.

phases.headline: Brown-Forman Says It Rejected Sazerac's Unsolicited Takeover Bid

events.whyItMatters: Nvidia takes about 4.5% of Naver through a ~$1bn new-share issue -- making the chipmaker Naver's third-largest shareholder behind the National Pension Service and BlackRock -- while Brookfield funds up to $9bn of a $10bn AI factory that lifts the GAK Sejong data centre from 55MW to 200MW by 2028. Naver gets sovereign-AI scale without carrying the capex alone; Nvidia gets another equity-linked customer locked into Blackwell and Vera Rubin.

phases.headline: Nvidia to invest $1 bil. in Naver for 4.5% stake, with Brookfield backing a $10 billion AI factory build at the GAK Sejong data centre

events.whyItMatters: A Blackstone-Brookfield-KKR consortium takes 49% of Kuwait Oil Company's 320km crude pipeline network under a 20.5-year lease-and-leaseback ('Project Peregrine'), handing KOC $7.85bn upfront against a $16bn headline value while it keeps 51% -- one of the largest Middle East infrastructure privatisations yet, and a large, long-duration, contracted asset for three listed alternative managers hunting scale in infrastructure.

phases.headline: Kuwait Oil Company Signs US$16.0 Billion Infrastructure Partnership Involving Its Crude Oil Pipeline Network With a Consortium Comprising Blackstone, Brookfield and KKR

events.whyItMatters: TransDigm pays ~$1.066bn cash for precision engineered-materials maker Prince & Izant, bought from Industrial Growth Partners -- its largest bolt-on of the year and a continuation of the debt-funded, high-margin proprietary-parts roll-up the whole TransDigm equity story rests on.

phases.headline: TransDigm Group Announces Agreement to Acquire Prince & Izant for Approximately $1.066 Billion in Cash

events.whyItMatters: Leonardo DRS pays $450m cash for Raft, a McLean, Virginia open-architecture mission-software firm, buying into multi-domain data fusion and AI rather than building it -- a step up the stack from hardware-centric defence electronics, funded from cash and the revolver, accretive to adjusted EPS in year one and carrying a ~$50m present-value tax benefit.

phases.headline: Leonardo DRS to Acquire Raft, Expanding Multi-Domain AI, Data Fusion and Mission Software Capabilities
